proposal.blind_spot: All kernels look identically DRAM-saturated, so the optimizer cannot tell whether a kernel already launches enough parallelism and sits at the true memory wall (only reducing bytes helps) or is under-occupied/latency-limited (re-parallelizing helps) - the exact decision whose wrong choice regressed the reduction kernels to 0.04-0.5x.

rationale.launch__waves_per_multiprocessor: HIGH -> grid already saturates the GPU; do not restructure parallelization (atomics/multi-pass reductions add pure traffic), only reduce bytes moved by fusing passes / LOW -> grid cannot fill the SMs; split the reduction or elementwise work into more blocks and raise ILP to hide latency
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH -> warps truly wait on global memory; with DRAM >90% the kernel is at the bandwidth wall, so attack only traffic volume/locality / LOW -> memory latency is not the dominant stall despite the high DRAM average; investigate synchronization/parallel structure of the reduction instead of memory-layout changes
